history.dynasty: None (modern; established by the saint Neem Karoli Baba)
history.period: Established 1962 (development began); Hanuman temple consecrated 15 June 1964; Baba's murti installed 15 June 1976
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: Kainchi Dham is NOT in Nainital town - it is the ashram and Hanuman temple of the saint Neem Karoli Baba at Kainchi village on the Nainital-Almora road in Nainital district, about 9 km from Bhowali and 17 km from Nainital. The name 'Kainchi' (scissors) is said to come from the scissor-like hairpin bends of the old hill road here. Developed from 1962 under Neem Karoli Baba with local devotee Shri Poornanand on land he donated; the Hanuman temple was consecrated on 15 June 1964 and Baba's own murti installed on 15 June 1976 (that date is now the annual Pratishtha Divas bhandara). The complex includes the temple, Baba's kutir, a small cave, meditation area, dharamshala and community kitchen. Neem Karoli Baba left his body in Vrindavan in 1973; visits by Steve Jobs (1974) and Mark Zuckerberg gave the ashram its international profile. Coordinates are village-level for Kainchi (Kosya Kutauli), Nainital - the ashram lies within the village (note: not a point-exact POI match). Primarily an ashram/temple complex; entry and darshan are free, phones are not allowed inside the main shrine, and there is no bookable overnight accommodation for tourists.

name: Kainchi Dham
town: Kainchi (CSV town 'Nainital' is approximate - the ashram is at Kainchi village, ~9 km from Bhowali and ~17 km from Nainital)
town_description: Kainchi is a small village on the Nainital-Almora highway in Nainital district at about 1,400 m, on the banks of the Kosi river amid pine forests. It is known almost entirely for the Kainchi Dham ashram of Neem Karoli Baba, which draws devotees and tourists year-round; Bhowali, 9 km away, is the nearest small town with shops and stays.

travel.road: On the Nainital-Almora highway (NH109); about 17-20 km from Nainital and 9 km from Bhowali; reachable by taxi, bus or shared jeep from Nainital, Haldwani and Delhi.

visitor_information.best_time: March to June for pleasant weather; 15 June is the annual bhandara (the busiest day). Winters (December-February) are cold with shorter timings.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: 6:00/7:00 AM to 6:00/7:00 PM (summer), reduced in winter (verify locally); one source lists 7:00-11:00 AM and 3:00-6:00 PM. Aarti around 6:45 AM and 6:45 PM. Free entry; phones not allowed inside the main shrine.
